text:
Matt H: Heads-up — KV cache hit rate on long-context routes dropped ~18% since last Tue. p99 latency creeping up and GPU-hours per minute spiked during the evening window. Anyone else seeing the same pattern?

Priya S: yep, saw it in the streaming cohort. Streaming share in NA-west jumped from 12% -> 39% last week; median context for streaming requests moved from ~2k -> ~5.6k tokens. That kills batching efficiency.

Aleks K: Is this mostly new customer traffic or an app change? Network or scheduler causing smaller batches?

Matt H: It's across several customers — looks like product teams started sending full docs instead of summaries. Also noticed more partial/keep-alive streams that prevent assembly into larger batches.

Sophia L: Quick numbers I pulled this morning: baseline GPU-hours/day for those pods was ~420; last 72h average is 468 (+11.4%). If the trend continues into seasonal peak, our simple projection shows ~+22% GPU-hours. Rough cost delta = ~ $2.5/hr * extra hours -> roughly $2.5k/week incremental across prod pools.

Priya S: TL;DR: longer contexts + streaming = lower KV cache hit rate -> more recompute of attention/kvs -> higher GPU-time per token. Also smaller effective batch sizes increase kernel overhead.

Matt H: Proposed mitigations (short-term):
- bump prefix/KV cache TTL for high-volume routes to improve hit locality
- increase batching window from `10ms` -> `30ms` for non-interactive streams (should be opt-in per route)
- enable compressed KV cache evictions (LRU tuned for long contexts)
- add a transient prewarm job to repopulate cache after deploys

Priya S: I ran a quick A/B sim: applying `30ms` window + TTL bump recovers ~60% of the lost batching efficiency in the sim, reducing projected GPU-hours growth from +22% down to +9%.

Aleks K: Longer-term: quantization profile + smaller attention kernels for >4k contexts and a dedicated streaming-optimized pool. But that requires infra and runtime changes. For immediate capacity we should consider reserving burst GPUs.

Matt H: Region constraints: eu-west quota is tight this quarter; we only have ~12 spare GPUs in account — requesting a quota lift will take ~3 business days. NA-west has spare capacity but network egress to EU is a concern for EU customers with data locality constraints.

Sophia L: Cost tradeoff if we do burst in NA-west and route EU traffic via dedicated private link: extra egress network cost estimate ~ $600/week vs estimated GPU cost savings of ~$1.2k/week. Worth it for short bursts.

Matt H: Quick ops runbook I propose:
1) change route config to opt-in `batching_window_ms=30` for streaming routes (config PR opened: `infra/4668`).
2) deploy a prewarm job that iterates hot prefixes every 5m for 48h.
3) request eu-west quota increase via cloud console (assign to @Aleks K).
4) schedule canary for TTL bump and measure KV hit rate over 6h.

Aleks K: on it — I filed the quota ticket (cloud support case `CS-9983`) and put a request in for temporary burst capacity.

infra-bot: automatic note: Deployment window opened for `infra/4668` at 1780456825. Canary cluster allocated: 2 gpus. Logs will stream to `gs://prod-logs/kvcache-canary/`.

Priya S: I'll run the PromQL queries and post graphs in the #observability thread. Query I used:
```
avg_over_time(gpu_hours_total[6h]) by (pool)
avg_over_time(kv_cache_hit_rate[6h]) by (route)
(rate(streaming_requests_total[5m]))
```

Matt H: If the canary looks good, let's roll to prod and keep burst reservation for 10 days. That should cover the expected seasonal uptick. Also we should notify sales about potential performance changes for enterprise customers.

Sophia L: I'll draft a short customer note and estimate cost impact per seat tier.

Aleks K: After canary, next steps: plan a streaming-optimized pool design doc. I'll schedule a 30-min sync Thu.

Matt H: Thanks all. Action items: @Aleks K file quota + burst (done), @Priya S post observability graphs, @Sophia L customer note draft, infra to monitor KV hit rate and p99 latencies every 30m. Ping me with any regressions. :thumbsup:
